To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the annual expenditures of medicine for hypertensive/diabetics elderly in Brazil were higher and inversly associated with physical activity levels and engagement in walking.
the annual expenditures of medicine used for controlling hypertension and/or diabetes of Brazilian elderly are higher and inversely related to physical activity levels and engagement in walking.
the annual expenditures of medicine for hypertensive and diabetic were higher and inversly associated with the physical activity level and walking engagement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the need to increase the level of physical activity in the elderly population and the importance of promoting walking as a form of physical activity.
the need for public policies that encourage and support elderly people to engage in physical activities, especially walking, in order to improve their health and quality of life.
the economic burden of chronic diseases in elderly population, especially in upper-middle income country.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the higher the PAL and the engagement in walking, the lower are the annual expenditures of medicine used to control hypertension and diabetes.
the elderly who were insufficiently physically active had a higher risk of being hypertensive and diabetic and had higher annual expenditures of medicines.
the elderly who are more active and walk more frequently are more likely to spend less on medicine for hypertension and diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physical activity level and walking engagement are important factors to reduce the costs of chronic diseases in the elderly.
the elderly with insufficiently physically activity and not walking have a greater risk for higher annual expenditures of medication use.
the elderly population with insufficient physical activity level and not engaged in walking had a higher annual cost of medicine use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
physical activity level and walking engagement are associated to medicine expenditures in hypertensive and diabetic population.
the elderly who are more physically active and walk more have lower drug expenditures for hypertension and diabetes.
physical activity and engagement walking are inversely associated with the annual cost of medicine use.
